crons.name: HL Strategy Lab — Weekly Deep Eval

quality.reason: Well-structured output with useful metadata (engagement counts, scores, direct links, timestamps) enabling quick triage, but the underlying tweet content is largely generic bullish chatter ('stay patient, much higher soon') with low analytical density, one low-engagement entry (4 likes), and a confusing $SOL/$MANIFEST ticker mismatch, so filtering quality needs improvement before this becomes high-value signal.

Well-structured digest with concrete metrics (PnL, win rate, signal strengths) and active SOL signals, but lacks analysis or action items, includes tangential news items, and the negative PnL over 72 trades warrants flagged insight rather than passive reporting.

Well-structured review with clear actionable signals: SOL's assigned strategy (stochastic) not ranking in top 10 while trend scores 75.21 suggests reassignment, plus ETH's flagged declining trend (78.7→63.1) and explicit position status make this genuine signal rather than noise.

Well-structured with clear formatting, timestamps, and position PnL tracking, but the flagged transaction sizes ($50-60K) fall well below genuine whale thresholds, suggesting alert thresholds are set too low and risk flooding users with retail-scale noise.

Well-structured daily review with specific metrics, trend deltas, volume stats, and clearly flagged actionable anomalies (news-agent crash, whale-monitor 0% uptime), though the contradictory whale-monitor score-vs-uptime pairing slightly muddies interpretation.

Well-structured digest with transparent methodology and adaptive fallback after API rate-limiting, but leaked internal reasoning text ('I have enough verified data') and the 500-char truncation prevent confirming actual paper content quality.

issues: Self-reported verification date (2026-08-19) postdates reviewer knowledge; tool and link availability cannot be independently confirmed

Depends entirely on third-party Homebrew taps (antoniorodr/memo, steipede/tap/imsg, steipete/tap/remindctl) rather than homebrew-core; personal taps are frequently abandoned or renamed with no fallback documented
Two-step 'brew tap user/repo && brew install user/repo/formula' pattern is unnecessary in modern Homebrew, which auto-taps via 'brew install user/repo/formula' (minor)

Exact CLI flags (memo new --body, remindctl add --due/--list with natural-language dates) are unverified against actual tool versions; interface drift is common in early-stage CLIs and could make examples fail
Intro promises AppleScript-based automation but all documented sections only cover CLIs; no AppleScript guidance appears in the reviewed content
Content was truncated mid-sentence in the iMessage permissions section, so the remainder of the doc and the references/*.md files cannot be assessed for dead links or accuracy
No documented uninstall/fallback or 'what to do if tap is gone' path, which matters for skills built on single-maintainer taps

No dated tools, versions, or URLs appear in the reviewed excerpt, so no dead links or deprecated APIs were found — but this is only the first 2000 chars and the actions table is cut off mid-entry ('right_clic'), so the remainder is unreviewed and may contain outdated parameters

Unverifiable claim: 'Claude was trained on both [element indices and pixel coordinates]' — Anthropic's computer-use-trained models are publicly documented around screenshot + pixel-coordinate clicking; there is no known training on AX-element-index clicking, so this claim is likely inaccurate and may mislead non-Claude and Claude usage alike

Overstated capability claim: background automation that 'does NOT move the user's cursor, steal keyboard focus, or switch Spaces' while 'clicking around in Safari in another Space' is dubious on macOS — CGEvent-based synthetic clicks move the cursor, and AX-level actions (AXPress) only partially avoid focus theft and frequently fail on background/unfocused windows; the doc presents a best case as a guarantee

Custom tool interface (`computer_use` with `element=N`, `capture_after=True`, mode `som|vision|ax`) does not match any public/vendor schema; if this wraps a real internal tool it's fine, but the parameters cannot be validated against any reference implementation, raising the risk that parts of the interface are hallucinated or drifted from the actual tool

Positive note on freshness: the terminology that is present (Set-of-Mark overlays, AX/accessibility tree, OpenAI-compatible local endpoints, per-model capability guidance) reflects current (2024–2025) computer-use agent practice and does not reference any sunset tools (e.g., legacy AppleScript-only automation is not recommended), so the visible content is stylistically current
Content truncated at 2000 chars mid-sentence — full body could not be reviewed, limiting freshness assessment
No external URLs in the visible excerpt, so dead-link verification is not possible (and not applicable to what was shown)
Claims like 'all 5 references/ files verified present' and 'fleet domains current' are internal assertions that cannot be independently confirmed from the excerpt

Review/update dates (Aug 23, 2026 and Jul 4, 2026) cannot be validated against reviewer knowledge; if these timestamps are erroneous or the doc has not actually been re-verified, staleness is undetectable from content alone
No deprecated tools or patterns detected: cron, Obsidian, LLM-driven optimization loops, and generate/critique/rewrite agent patterns are all currently standard
Subsystem table count (5) matches the stated verified file count — internally consistent, but file existence is unverifiable
All three referenced tools (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI @openai/codex, OpenCode) are actively maintained; no deprecated or dead tools detected in the visible content

No URLs present in this excerpt, so link rot cannot be fully assessed — the referenced files (references/claude-code.md, references/codex.md, references/opencode.md) are not shown and may contain outdated CLI flags or commands
Claude Code 'print mode' terminology is accurate but evolving rapidly; flag names like -p/--print should be re-verified against current CLI docs
Codex CLI subcommands (e.g., exec for one-shot/background tasks) have changed across releases in 2025; the reference file should be checked for current command syntax
'OpenCode' naming is ambiguous (sst/opencode vs. older Go-based project of the same name); the description matches the active sst/opencode project but a canonical repo URL would reduce ambiguity
Dependency on hermes-agent skill and delegate_task tool is internal and cannot be externally verified for freshness
No version numbers, last-verified dates, or changelog references, making future freshness audits harder

Tool naming mismatch: doc references 'cua-driver' CLI/commands ('cua-driver skills install', '~/.cua-driver/skills/cua-driver') but links to github.com/trycua/cua, whose package and CLI are actually 'cua'; the install command, skills mechanism, and directory path are unverifiable or invented

Forward-looking roadmap claim ('Hermes autodetection is a planned cua-driver follow-up') with a manual symlink workaround — this is exactly the kind of instruction that goes stale immediately once (or if never) the feature ships; it needs a date-stamped status check

Misleading claim 'There is no Anthropic-native schema to learn': Anthropic does ship a native computer-use tool schema (screenshot/coordinate-based); the wrapper merely hides it, so the phrasing may confuse readers maintaining Anthropic integrations

Inaccurate model claim: 'Claude was trained on both' — Claude's computer-use training is screenshot+coordinate-based; element-index (SoM/AX-tree) targeting is not an Anthropic-trained pattern, so this guidance may mislead on which models need indices

Only one external link (repo URL) and it's a soft reference; no link to actual action reference, MCP tool docs, or the 'Cua skill' it depends on, so the documented action vocabulary cannot be validated against any upstream source
Body is truncated mid-Step-2 ('**Step'), so remaining workflow steps and any deprecated actions beyond the excerpt are unreviewed

SoM capture + accessibility-tree indexing is a current pattern (cogagent/OS-Copilot/OmniParser lineage), but nothing in the doc confirms the wrapper still matches the underlying cua API surface, which has iterated rapidly through 2025
Core git content (merge/rebase conflicts, worktrees, merge-queue arbiter analogy, neutral-reconciler pattern) is current and not deprecated — the staleness risk is concentrated in tool integrations.

References `delegate_task` as the subagent-spawning tool; public Claude Code tooling uses Task/Agent for this. If `delegate_task` is a live internal tool this is fine, otherwise the name needs updating.

Depends on `hermes kanban show <task-id>` CLI — could not verify this tool exists or is still current; if the hermes/kanban stack has been retired, Prerequisites and the spawned-agent workflow are broken.
References `kanban_create(title=..., assignee="reconciler", parents=[...])` — tool name and kwarg signature (especially `parents`) should be verified against the current kanban API.
No URLs appear in the excerpt, so no dead-link risk, but the Prerequisites section has a hard dependency on the unverifiable kanban/hermes toolchain.
Minor: assumes 'third profile' concept from the kanban system is still meaningful; jargon should be checked for consistency with current tooling docs.
